newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Salomon donwgrades China Eastern Airlines.
newsitem.headline: Salomon donwgrades China Eastern Airlines.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said it has upgraded its earning estimate for China Eastern Airlines Corp Ltd but downgraded its share recommendation to Hold from Buy.
The carrier is expected to announce calendar 1996 earnings on April 29.

Salomon previously forecast a profit of Chinese Renminbi 503 million based on expectations of a difficult second half. Its analysts now think the second half was not as bad as feared and have increased the profit forecast by 12 percent to Rmb565 million for calendar 1966.

In March, Salomon started its coverage of China Eastern with a Buy rating. That has now been downgraded to Hold, reflecting the strong price performance of the stock over the past two months, it said in its latest report on the airline.

The report also said it expects the Shanghai-based carrier, which is one of China's three largest airlines and the first Chinese carrier to be listed, to be a major beneficiary of the Chinese government's intention to bring domestic airfares in line with the price charged to foreigners.

A 20 percent increase in domestic yields is expected in the first year, the report said. But with such a large fare increase, demand is likely to soften and the annualised Revenue Passenger Kilometre (RPK) growth rate has been halved from 12 percent to six percent.
The report expects higher fares on 40 percent of China Eastern's total business.
Salomon analysts estimate big rises in China Eastern's operating statistics.
On yield analysis, Salomons expect overall yield per RPK to rise from 6.516 in 1995 to 6.556 in 1996, 6.744 in 1997 and 6.901 in 1998.
Total RPKs in 1995 were 7,733 and are estimated to rise to 8,586 in 1996, 9,249 in 1997 and 9,965 in 1998.
Cargo Tonne Kms in 1995 was 309.6 and is estimated to rise to 335.1 in 1996, 364.4 in 1997 and to 415.4 in 1998.
Total Available Tonne Kilometres (ATKs) are expected to rise then fall.
In 1995 total ATKs was 6.6 and are estimated to rise to 13.5 in 1996, 11.6 in 1997 and 10.7 in 1998. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
